newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper struggling, aluminium eyes upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper struggling, aluminium eyes upside.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices will struggle to overcome stiff resistance in the $2,440/50 area against an indifferent technical background, analysts said.
But aluminium, having swept past previous resistance on Monday, now targets the $1,605 and then $1,630 levels if its upwards momentum holds up, they added.
COPPER - Near-term technical indicators were generally pointing lower for copper and consolidation or even a downward drift appeared to be on the cards, analysts said.

"Technically, prices have run into resistance at $2,440 and could be turned lower as the moving averages have made a bearish cross. Support is seen at $2,420, $2,400 and $2,375," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.

Analyst William Adams of Rudolf Wolff noted the market's focus has been on the cash/threes spread with little interest in three months prices, which failed in a recent attempt to breach the key $2,440-$2,450 area.
"Technically we are still trading within the flag formation, which means the base around $2,350 is not yet secure," Adams said.
An LME stock rise of 3,175 tonnes on Tuesday morning was also not supportive. At 0900 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,410/$2,414 per tonne, compared to $2,422 at Monday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - Having broken above $1,600 in late Monday trading, prices had potential to continue exploring the upside, analysts said.
Clearance of the $1,602 level targeted the recent high of $1,628 from June 11, analysts said.
Before that, a June 13 gap between $1,608 and $1,612 would be filled.
Fundamental news was generally supportive, analysts said.
"Continued talk of tightness in Japan and also the endless stream of metal out of LME warehouses is leading some to question their recent bearish stance," said a GNI research commodity report.
LME stocks declined by 975 tonnes on Tuesday morning, after falling by 2,575 tonnes on Monday.
At 0900 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,605/$1,607, versus $1,598.
